order_description: Respiratory assist device, bi-level pressure capability, without backup rate feature, used with noninvasive interface, e.g., nasal or facial mask (intermittent assist device with continuous positive airway pressure device)

candidates.title: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

selection_reason: The order is E0470 (bi-level RAD without backup rate) for a patient with severe OSA (AHI 32, central/mixed apneas 8%, not >50%), intolerant of CPAP (E0601) despite mask and pressure changes. L33718 governs E0470 for OSA: it requires E0601 tried and proven ineffective, which the record documents. The L33800 RAD policy applies to restrictive, CSA/CompSA, hypoventilation, or COPD-related CRF, none of which fit here, and L33405 is only a sleep testing policy.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has an in-person clinical evaluation by the treating practitioner prior to the sleep test to assess the beneficiary for obstructive sleep apnea.
criteria.explanation: The sleep test (attended in-laboratory polysomnography for suspected OSA) was on 2026-08-26 (R22). The only earlier practitioner encounters in the record are contraception care visits, dental care and a general examination on 2025-06-27 (R15), and none documents an in-person evaluation assessing the patient for obstructive sleep apnea before the sleep test. The first documented OSA evaluations (R75, R76) come after the sleep test. The record does not document the required pre-test evaluation, so this criterion cannot be confirmed.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has a sleep test that meets either of the following criteria (1 or 2): 1. The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) or Respiratory Disturbance Index (RDI) is greater than or equal to 15 events per hour with a minimum of 30 events; or, 2. The AHI or RDI is greater than or equal to 5 and less than or equal to 14 events per hour with a minimum of 10 events and documentation of excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorders, or insomnia; or hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke.
criteria.explanation: Alternative 1 applies. The attended in-laboratory polysomnography (Type I study) on 2026-08-26 recorded an AHI of 32 events/hour (R43), with 198 events over 6.2 hours of sleep (R65). That is at or above 15 events per hour with well over 30 events, so the sleep test meets alternative 1 and alternative 2 is not needed.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary and/or their caregiver has received instruction from the supplier of the device in the proper use and care of the equipment.
criteria.explanation: The record shows a home CPAP unit (R12), use data from a device download (R44), and mask refitting and pressure adjustment (R75). It does not document that the supplier instructed the patient or a caregiver in the proper use and care of the equipment, so this criterion cannot be confirmed.

criteria.policy_text: An E0601 has been tried and proven ineffective based on a therapeutic trial conducted in either a facility or in a home setting. Ineffective is defined as documented failure to meet therapeutic goals using an E0601 during the titration portion of a facility-based study or during home use despite optimal therapy (i.e., proper mask selection and fitting and appropriate pressure settings).
criteria.explanation: The home trial is a home-setting trial, which the criterion allows. CPAP was started on 2026-09-10 (R75). The sleep medicine note of 2026-12-29 documents mask refitting (nasal pillows, then a full-face mask), heated humidification and pressure adjustment, which address mask selection and fitting and pressure settings (R75). Despite this, the device download shows use on only 12 of the last 30 nights, averaging 2.6 hours on nights used (R44, R50), which fails the therapeutic adherence goal. Residual AHI on CPAP is 5/h (R60). The patient reports she cannot tolerate CPAP (R75). The record therefore documents failure of the E0601 trial despite optimal therapy. The record describes this as CPAP intolerance rather than using the word ineffective, but the documented findings meet the definition.

criteria.policy_text: A sleep test (Type I, II, III, IV, Other) that meets the Medicare requirements for a valid sleep test as outlined in NCD 240.4.1 and the applicable A/B MAC LCD and Billing and Coding article.
criteria.explanation: The sleep test is an attended in-laboratory polysomnography, which is a Type I study, performed with a sleep center technologist (R22). A signed-off report with severity classification, AHI, central and mixed apnea percentage and SpO2 nadir is on file (R65). The record supports the test as a valid Type I study.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test results meet the coverage criteria in effect for the date of service of the claim for the PAP device.
criteria.explanation: The 2026-08-26 polysomnography shows an AHI of 32 events/hour with 198 events over 6.2 hours of sleep (R43, R65). These results meet the AHI criterion of at least 15 events per hour with at least 30 events under I.B.1.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test is ordered by the beneficiary's treating practitioner.
criteria.explanation: The record documents that the polysomnography was performed for suspected obstructive sleep apnea (R22) and reported (R65), but it does not document who ordered the sleep test or that the ordering practitioner was the treating practitioner. The requirement is a specific action by a specific person, so it cannot be confirmed from the record.

decision_explanation: Criterion I.B (sleep test severity), II.D (failed E0601 trial despite optimal mask and pressure therapy) and Sleep Tests.1 and Sleep Tests.3 are met. No criterion is shown to be not met. However, the record does not document an in-person OSA evaluation by the treating practitioner before the sleep test (I.A), does not document supplier instruction in the proper use and care of the device (I.C), and does not document who ordered the sleep test (Sleep Tests.4). Because these required items are missing, coverage cannot be confirmed.
